messages.text: England's Carse unavailable for Lord's Test after nightclub incident

metadata.summary: England fast bowler Brydon Carse has been withdrawn from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan at Lord's from Thursday following an incident outside a Derby nightclub that is being investigated by the Cricket Regulator.
metadata.content: Brydon Carse to miss England's second Test vs Pakistan as Cricket Regulator conducts investigation into nightclub incident | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Brydon Carse to miss England's second Test vs Pakistan as Cricket Regulator conducts investigation into nightclub incident Video footage emerged of handcuffed Carse being led away by police on Saturday night; fast bowler had been out celebrating victory for Durham in County Championship after being released by England to play in game; Sonny Baker replaces Carse in squad for Lord’s Test from Thursday Monday 24 August 2026 16:57, UK Image: England fast bowler Brydon Carse has been withdrawn from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan at Lord's following an incident outside a Derby nightclub England fast bowler Brydon Carse has been withdrawn from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan at Lord's from Thursday following an incident outside a Derby nightclub that is being investigated by the Cricket Regulator. Video footage emerged of a handcuffed Carse being led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship. Carse was seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background. metadata.summary: While he won neither of the race formats across the Zandvoort Sprint weekend, Kimi Antonelli increased his overall world championship lead at the Dutch Grand Prix as Formula 1 returned from its summer break.
metadata.content: Lando Norris: Is McLaren driver now Kimi Antonelli's biggest threat for 2026 F1 world title after Dutch GP win? | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Lando Norris: Is McLaren driver now Kimi Antonelli's biggest threat for 2026 F1 world title after Dutch GP win? Back-to-back wins for Lando Norris and McLaren has raised the spectre of the world champions yet having a significant say in this year's Drivers' Championship fight; watch the Italian Grand Prix at Monza live on Sky Sports F1 on September 4-6 Monday 24 August 2026 15:48, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris hunted down Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton to take the race lead at the Dutch Grand Prix. While he won neither of the race formats across the Zandvoort Sprint weekend, Kimi Antonelli increased his overall world championship lead at the Dutch Grand Prix as Formula 1 returned from its summer break. The Mercedes driver now leads both team-mate George Russell and Ferrari rival Lewis Hamilton by 59 points, the second-largest advantage Antonelli has enjoyed at the top of the Drivers' Championship so far this season. But Antonelli's advantage over the driver now occupying fourth place in the standings was cut by a further eight points, following reigning champion Lando Norris' second successive Grand Prix victory, which moved him to within 83 points of the championship lead. metadata.summary: St Helens captain Jackson Hastings' season could be over after being handed a three-match ban for violent conduct following his sending off in their win over Castleford Tigers on Saturday.
metadata.content: Jackson Hastings: St Helens captain given three-game ban for violent conduct that could end his season | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to content Jackson Hastings: St Helens captain given three-game ban for violent conduct that could end his season St Helens keep their play-off hopes alive with victory over Castleford, despite Jackson Hastings' sending off for violent conduct; his Grade E offence for punching the Tigers' Tyler Dupree carries a three-game ban, meaning his season could be over if Saints fail to qualify Monday 24 August 2026 13:22, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jackson Hastings is sent off for punching Tyler Dupree, then clashes continue off the pitch between St Helens and Castleford Tigers. St Helens captain Jackson Hastings' season could be over after being handed a three-match ban for violent conduct following his sending off in their win over Castleford Tigers on Saturday. Hastings was dismissed in the first half of the 36-12 victory after punching Castleford's Tyler Dupree, who was sin-binned for the same incident. Commenting on Hastings' dismissal, Castleford director of rugby Chris Chester told Sky Sports : "Scott Murrell just jumped (in the way of Dupree).
